name: Waacking
notes: Waacking style pack (Doc 04 template). Born as 'punking' in early-1970s Los Angeles Black and Latino gay clubs — a dance of defiant glamour that reclaimed an insult and turned club nights into cinema. Spread to the world by Tyrone 'The Bone' Proctor and Soul Train. Design truths: the whack is the namesake but the POSE is the soul — old-Hollywood glamour, the face fully in it; musicality is disco storytelling (strings, horns, drama); and the queer club origin is the root of the style, honored in curriculum, not mentioned as trivia.

seasons.finale: Film 60 seconds of the disco groove — strut alive, on beat, chin up like the club is watching.
Film 8 counts of clean overhead whacks both arms — elbow leads, strikes land ON the beat.
Film a pose run: four poses in 8 counts, every line finished, face committed.
Film 30 seconds hitting the orchestration — whack the horns, melt with the strings, pose the break.
Perform one disco track for humans — a class, a circle, a living room runway. Glamour requires witnesses.

attributes.name: Shoulder freedom L1
attributes.test: 20 full backstroke arm circles each side, smooth, shoulders never hiking

attributes.name: Wrist articulation L1
attributes.test: 20 clean wrist circles each hand with the arm extended overhead, elbow still

attributes.name: Club stamina L1
attributes.test: one full disco track of continuous groove and arm work, breathing conversational

nodes.name: Disco time — strings, horns, four on the floor
checkpoints: waacking lives on disco: 110-130 BPM, orchestral, dramatic
the whack lands ON the beat; the pose lives BETWEEN beats
listen for the arrangement — strings and horns are your cues, not just the drums

nodes.name: Musical storytelling — dancing the arrangement
checkpoints: whack the horn stabs, melt with the strings, freeze the break
every song is a scene; you are the leading lady or the villain — choose
dynamics beat speed: one perfectly placed strike outdramas twenty

nodes.name: Punking: the clubs that made it (LA, early 1970s)
checkpoints: born in Los Angeles' Black and Latino gay clubs in the early 1970s — first called punking, an insult reclaimed and worn as armor
the glamour vocabulary channeled old-Hollywood divas — the club was the movie screen
the queer club origin is the ROOT of this dance; carrying the style means carrying that history with respect

nodes.name: Tyrone Proctor and the world stage
checkpoints: Tyrone 'The Bone' Proctor carried waacking onto Soul Train and around the world
the Outrageous Waack Dancers put the style on stages; today's teachers keep the lineage alive
watch original-era footage before stylizing your own — the source sets the standard

nodes.name: The revival — battles, classes, and keeping the root
checkpoints: waacking battles run worldwide today (Juste Debout and the club scenes that never stopped)
learn from teachers who credit the clubs and name the pioneers
the style is welcome to everyone BECAUSE it came from people who weren't welcomed — never flip that upside down

nodes.name: The disco strut
nodes.anchor: the walk that says you belong here
checkpoints: chest lifted, chin level, steps land on the beat with intention
hips travel, shoulders answer — the groove is the runway
eyes up: waacking never looks at the floor
mistakes: shy steps — the strut is a declaration
grooving down like hip hop; disco carries you UP

nodes.name: The whack (overhead strikes)
nodes.origin: the style's namesake strike, forged in the LA punking clubs
nodes.anchor: a week to learn, a year to make it sing
checkpoints: the elbow leads; the forearm whips over the head and past the ear
the strike lands ON the beat, then the arm recovers soft — hard-soft is the texture
wrists stay alive; dead hands kill the line
alternate arms without the groove stalling
mistakes: swinging from the shoulder like a windmill — the whack is a whip, not a swing
hitting yourself in the head (everyone does once; elbows wider)

nodes.name: Rolls & figure-8s
checkpoints: consecutive whacks chain into rolls — the arms draw ribbons around the head
double-time the arms while the strut stays on the beat
the pattern breathes: roll, roll, STRIKE
mistakes: speed without shape — every rotation still has a line

nodes.name: Poses & lines
nodes.origin: old-Hollywood glamour, channeled through the club
checkpoints: a pose is a finished photograph: line complete from fingertips to face
frame the face — hands present it, chin sells it
hold a full beat minimum; a rushed pose is a missed pose
the face is IN the pose: bored eyes ruin perfect lines
mistakes: checking the mirror mid-pose — the camera is out THERE

nodes.name: The runway walk
checkpoints: strut + pose = runway: travel, plant, photograph, travel
corners are moments — turn like the room turned with you
own the space you cross; the walk claims the floor

nodes.name: One disco track — filmed
checkpoints: one full track: whacks on beat, at least four finished poses, drama honored
commit to a character for the whole song
watch it back for FACE first, arms second

nodes.name: Spotlight — perform for humans
checkpoints: a class, a circle, or a living-room runway with an audience of one — witnessed
say where the style came from if anyone asks — that's part of performing it
glamour is generosity: give the room a show
